PullRequest.Title: Agents window: center the Customizations label and count
PullRequest.Body: ## Summary - Vertically align the Customizations header label and total count in the Agents window sidebar. - Use a natural header line-height and a font-relative optical adjustment for the smaller digits, preserving the count's size, weight, and color. ## Validation - `npm run build-fast -- --client-only` — passed. - `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/sessions/test/browser/customizationsToolbar.test.ts --reporter dot` — passed, 5 tests. - `npm run stylelint -- src/vs/sessions/contrib/sessions/browser/media/customizationsToolbar.css` — passed. - `git diff --check` — passed. - Ad hoc Playwright/Chromium validation — passed 18 visible-glyph alignment checks across expanded/collapsed states, counts of 1/113/9999, and three inherited line-heights. Measured glyph-center differences were below 0.15 CSS pixels; typography was unchanged. To check manually, expand and collapse the Customizations sidebar section and confirm its smaller total count appears vertically centered with the bold label. ## Visual evidence Before/after comparison to be attached manually by the author. The prepared comparison uses isolated Chromium rendering with the original and updated component CSS, macOS system font, and a count of 113. It is not a live workbench screenshot. ## Review status - No actionable findings in the scoped review. - Live workbench and other-platform font rendering were not exercised.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open the Agents window with the Customizations sidebar section visible
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The widget constructs one header and the browser resolves its static typography during the existing style/layout pass before the sidebar is displayed. The added normal line-height and static translate do not add script, layout reads, or another render pass.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One Customizations header per widget, independent of the number of sessions or customization items.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Single browser main-thread render; no queue, fan-out, or parallel work is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache or cache key is involved; cold and subsequent renders use the same static stylesheet rules.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the complete CSS diff and the traced widget construction path: only one static header element receives these rules.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Browser/font-specific line metrics may slightly alter the header geometry, but the diff adds no repeated or scaling work.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The change participates in the existing style/layout pass and does not increase work cardinality or add a synchronous layout boundary.

Scenarios.Scenario: Customization counts change while the section is collapsed
Scenarios.CriticalPath: An existing observable updates the single count span's text and hidden class. The new transform is already part of its computed style and introduces no additional callback, geometry read, or per-item operation.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One span per widget per observable count update; customization collection size does not multiply styled nodes.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Observable updates and DOM mutation run serially on the browser main thread; the diff does not change scheduling or coalescing.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Counts come from existing observable models; the CSS change neither adds reads nor changes cold/warm model behavior.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that the changed rules apply to exactly the existing total-count span and do not alter update frequency.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact paint/compositing choices vary by browser, but a static 2D transform on one small span is not evidence of a separately promoted layer or meaningful retained cost.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Update cardinality and DOM mutation behavior are unchanged, with no proven new layout, paint, or memory scaling mechanism.

Scenarios.Scenario: Collapse, expand, or resize the Customizations sidebar section
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Existing code reads header offsetHeight/scrollHeight and lays out the split view. The line-height may alter the resulting static header height, but the diff adds no geometry read-after-write, nested relayout, or extra scanDomNode call.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One header and one split-view layout per user collapse/expand or host resize event; unchanged by customization count.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous, serialized sidebar layout on the main thread; no new concurrency or burst is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No caching applies to CSS geometry; both initial and repeated layouts reuse the same DOM and stylesheet.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence after tracing collapsedHeight, desiredHeight, and layout callers in the sidebar split-view path.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The exact computed normal line-height depends on platform font metrics, but it affects geometry rather than the amount or frequency of layout work.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Existing layout reads remain unchanged and the CSS adjustment does not introduce a scaling or repeated-work mechanism.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed the complete one-file CSS diff and traced header creation, observable count updates, collapse/expand behavior, and split-view layout. The typography-only changes affect one static header/count pair and introduce no additional script work, expensive boundary, fan-out, retention, forced-layout sequence, or realistic scaling mechanism. No performance findings were submitted.
